facts.statement: The genus Pachycheilosuchus was named and described by Jack Rogers in 2003.
facts.quote: This genus was named and described by Jack Rogers in 2003.

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus lived in Texas, United States, during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Pachycheilosuchus (meaning "thick lipped crocodile") is an extinct genus of neosuchian from the Early Cretaceous of Texas, United States.

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus is notable for having procoelous vertebrae, a feature otherwise found only in derived eusuchian crocodilians.
facts.quote: this crocodylomorph is notable for its procoelous vertebrae, otherwise found only in derived eusuchian crocodilians

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus was not a large crocodylomorph, with the longest collected thigh bone measuring only 91.2 millimeters.
facts.quote: It was not a large crocodylomorph; for example, of the collected thigh bones, the longest measured only 91.2 millimeters long (3.59 in).

facts.statement: A 49 millimeter-long crocodyloid egg recovered with fossils suggests that some individuals were sexually mature at a length of 63.5 centimeters.
facts.quote: Additionally, a 49 millimeter-long (1.9 in) crocodyloid egg was recovered with the skeletal fossils, and is of reasonable size to have come from an individual with a length of 63.5 centimeters, suggesting that some of the individuals were sexually mature.

facts.statement: A puncture mark measuring 5 millimeters by 6.5 millimeters on a maxilla was probably made by a larger predator.
facts.quote: One maxilla has an oval puncture mark, 5 millimeters by 6.5 millimeters (0.2 by 0.26 in), probably made by a larger predator.

facts.statement: The ulna, the major bone of the forearm, was strongly curved in Pachycheilosuchus.
facts.quote: The ulna, the major bone of the forearm, is strongly curved.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the previously known "Glen Rose Form" represents a single species or multiple forms, as some fossils lack the defining features of Pachycheilosuchus.
facts.quote: With the description of Pachycheilosuchus, it appears that the "Glen Rose Form" had been chimeric; the skull and the two skeletons lack the lipped jaw and procoelous vertebrae, and so are not Pachycheilosuchus but an undescribed form, but at least some of the isolated remains are Pachycheilosuchus.

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous (Cretácico Inferior).
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Inferior

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus is classified within the family Hylaeochampsidae.
facts.quote: familia: Hylaeochampsidae

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus had a short and flat snout.
facts.quote: El hocico era corto y plano.

facts.statement: Procoelous vertebrae articulate with a concave anterior surface and a convex posterior surface.
facts.quote: Las vértebras procélicas tienen un tipo de articulación basada en la forma de las caras anterior y posterior del centro vertebral.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Pachycheilosuchus likely evolved procoely independently because it lacked other eusuchian characteristics.
facts.quote: Debido a esta diferencia, y ya que Pachycheilosuchus no tenía varias de las demás características de los eusuquios, es probable que haya evolucionado la condición procélica independientemente.

facts.statement: Fossils of crocodylomorphs from Glen Rose were previously known under the informal designation "Glen Rose form".
facts.quote: Anteriormente, los fósiles de crocodilomorfos de Glen Rose habían sido conocidos bajo la designación informal de "forma de Glen Rose".

facts.statement: Fossils known as the "Glen Rose form" included a skull at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History and two partial skeletons at the Texas Memorial Museum, along with isolated bones.
facts.quote: Los fósiles conocidos con este nombre incluían un cráneo en el Museo Nacional de Historia Natural del Instituto Smithsoniano y dos esqueletos parciales en el Museo Memorial de Texas, junto con huesos aislados.

facts.statement: With the description of Pachycheilosuchus, it appears that the "Glen Rose form" was a paleontological chimera.
facts.quote: Con la descripción de Pachycheilosuchus, parece que la "forma de Glen Rose" era una quimera paleontológica

facts.statement: The skull and two skeletons lacked the "lip" jaw and procervical vertebrae, meaning they do not belong to Pachycheilosuchus but to an undescribed form.
facts.quote: el cráneo y los dos esqueletos carecían de la mandíbula con "labio" y las vértebras procélicas, y por tanto no pertenecen a Pachycheilosuchus sino a una forma aún sin describir

facts.statement: However, some of the isolated bones do belong to Pachycheilosuchus.
facts.quote: aunque algunos de los huesos aislados sí son de Pachycheilosuchus

facts.statement: Therefore, there were at least two crocodylomorphs in the Glen Rose Formation.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, habría al menos dos crocodilomorfos en la Formación Glen Rose.

facts.statement: The parent group of Pachycheilosuchus is Hylaeochampsidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hylaeochampsidae

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus belongs to the family Hylaeochampsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Hylaeochampsidae

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Pachycheilosuchus lived during the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)
